title: Cylindrical base
spec: Create a cylindrical base by first setting up a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on a single face. Within this face, draw a single loop, and within this loop, draw a circle centered at coordinates (0.0079, 0.0079) with a radius of 0.0079. Apply a scaling factor of 0.0158 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] degrees and translating it using the translation vector [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. Extrude the transformed sketch along the normal direction by 0.75 units to create a solid body. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. The final dimensions of the cylindrical base are 0.015789473684210527 units in length, 0.015789473684210527 units in width, and 0.75 units in height.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Define the initial coordinate system
workplane = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the base of the cylinder
workplane = workplane.center(0.0079, 0.0079).circle(0.0079)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
r = workplane.extrude(0.75, taper=0.0158)

# The final model is stored in 'r'

lanes.label: GLM-5.3 Flash (high)
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Outer cylinder
outer = cq.Workplane("XY").circle(0.0079).extrude(0.75)

# Inner hole (tube)
inner = cq.Workplane("XY").circle(0.0060).extrude(0.75)

r = outer.cut(inner)
